title: [YouPass Collect] - Workforce distribution across sectors 1980 vs 2010
prompt: The charts below show the percentage of workers in three sectors across four countries in 1980 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the proportion of workers employed in agriculture, industry, and services across four countries in 1980 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, agricultural and services employment declined across all four nations over the 30-year period, while industrial workforces expanded in Germany, the USA, and Japan, though not in China. Additionally, China's agricultural sector remained considerably larger than the others throughout, whereas Germany and Japan recorded the highest industrial employment by 2010.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the declining sectors, agricultural employment fell across all countries, though the extent varied significantly. China experienced the steepest drop, from 70% in 1980 to 50% in 2010, while the figures for Japan, the USA, and Germany declined more modestly, from 11% to 10%, 8% to 6%, and 4% to 2%, respectively. Similarly, the services sector contracted in all four nations, with China recording the sharpest fall from 49% to 20%, followed by Japan (39% to 28%), the USA (47% to 37%), and Germany (50% to 40%).

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, industrial employment followed a different trajectory. In 1980, Germany led with 60%, followed by the USA at 52%, Japan at 49%, and China at 40%. By 2010, Germany and Japan had experienced substantial growth, reaching 80% and 78% respectively, while the USA's figure rose to 70%. Notably, China's industrial workforce remained unchanged at 40%, making it the only country where this sector did not expand.
